title: Arjuna's austerities
hook: on the mountain, a thin old ascetic tells Arjuna to throw away his bow, and Arjuna won't

segments.voice: Yesterday Vyasa came to the forest, and your line was Vana: exile. The waiting became a plan, and Arjuna set out alone. Did you use a stretch of waiting to prepare? Day seven hundred eighty-two.

Stop. The word rings out across a mountain slope in the north, and Arjuna stops. He has walked a long way, bow in hand, quiver on his back, toward a peak the epic calls Indrakila. Under a tree sits an ascetic, thin, matted hair, glowing with the strength of long discipline. And the ascetic looks at the armed young man and asks, more or less: what are you doing with those? This is a place of peace. Today the first test of Arjuna's austerities, and it doesn't look like a test at all.
screen: `STOP.` → `AN ASCETIC UNDER A TREE.` → `WHAT ARE YOU DOING WITH THOSE?`

segments.voice: The ascetic goes on. Here, he says, live peaceful seekers who have left anger behind. There's no need for weapons in this place. Throw away your bow. You've already reached a high state. It's a tempting offer, and he makes it again and again. But Arjuna won't put the bow down. He tells the ascetic he won't leave his brothers waiting in the forest and go off to some peaceful world without the weapons he came for. Then the ascetic shows who he really is. He's Indra, king of the gods, and Arjuna's own father in the story. He's pleased, and he offers his son a boon: ask for anything. Arjuna asks for weapons. And Indra answers: first, you must see Shiva, the three-eyed god who holds the trident. When you've seen him, I'll give you my own weapons. So the first lesson of Arjuna's austerities is a surprising one. The test isn't whether he can give everything up. It's whether he knows what he came for. Indra's offer of peace sounds holy, and in another life it might be his path. But Arjuna has a purpose, a family in the forest and a promise to keep, and he holds onto it even when a radiant ascetic tells him to let it go. Austerity, in this story, doesn't start with fasting. It starts with being clear about why you're there.
screen: `THROW AWAY YOUR BOW.` · `ARJUNA HOLDS ON.` · `IT WAS INDRA ALL ALONG.` · then, large: `FIRST, YOU MUST SEE SHIVA.`

segments.voice: Let yourself settle, and feel the weight of your body resting. Bring to mind something you're working toward right now, small or large. A task, a change, a person you're trying to show up for. Breathe in, and ask: why am I doing this? Breathe out, and let the answer be simple. If other voices come, telling you to drop it, let them pass like weather on a mountain. Come back to the why. If you pray, you can hold that purpose in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Arjuna's austerities. They begin on a mountain, where an ascetic tells him to throw away his bow, and Arjuna remembers why he came.
Your line: remember why you came. Today, before you start something, say to yourself in a few words why you're doing it. Day seven hundred eighty-two.

howItsDone: Retellings of the Mahabharata follow Arjuna to the mountain, where Indra tests him in disguise before sending him to seek Shiva; the episode is part of the long tradition of tapas, ascetic effort, in Hindu stories.

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli that the voice saying 'Stop' comes from the sky or from the ascetic, and the ascetic's description (lean, matted locks, tawny).

Indra as Arjuna's father is the epic's own account of Arjuna's birth; confirm framing.
